text.p: Greenpeace environmental group on Monday charged the Mexican Green Ecology Party (PVEM) with illegally using the activist group's logo and materials during a campaign ahead of upcoming Mexican elections.

Greenpeace complained the PVEM had used Greenpeace material during its television ads in the run-up to the July 6 mid-term elections, when Mexicans elect most of a new Congress, several state governors and a Mexico City mayor.
Greenpeace leveled the charges before Mexico's highest electoral body, which has the power to levy fines to political parties for campaign irregularities.
"Our organisation does not support, sponsor or receive financial aid from any political party or organisation," Monique Mitastein, head of Greenpeace in Mexico, told reporters.
"The PVEM's television campaign has caused considerable harm to our moral reputation," she said.
Greenpeace demanded a public apology from the party.
The PVEM has gained support in the polluted capital city and is currently running fourth in the polls with about seven to eight percent support.
